package_info.package_manager: standalone tool (not a package manager, but used in attack chain)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (tool usage, not a library vulnerability)
package_info.why_malicious: The attack leverages the recollapse tool to automate input fuzzing and Unicode encoding of phone numbers, exploiting normalization inconsistencies in OpenAI's account signup API. This enables mass creation of accounts using variants of the same phone number, bypassing uniqueness validation and abusing free credit allocation.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (API request manipulation during account signup)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the attacker modifies the phone_number field in the intercepted API request by prepending leading zeros, which alters the input format, bypasses upstream uniqueness validation, and results in successful registration of multiple accounts with the same underlying phone number.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Manipulating phone number formatting with leading zeros is a known evasion technique to defeat naive uniqueness checks. Legitimate users do not alter phone numbers in this way during signup.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal account creation expects phone numbers to be normalized (removing leading zeros) and validated for uniqueness before account creation. Here, the system fails to normalize before checking, allowing bypass.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some international dialing conventions may use leading zeros, but in this context, the intent is to subvert validation, not to comply with legitimate formatting.
key_indicators: Phone numbers with unexpected leading zeros in signup requests
Multiple accounts registered with phone numbers that normalize to the same value
API requests to /dashboard/onboarding/phone/verify with phone_number fields differing only by leading zeros

execution_context.trigger: runtime (API request manipulation during account signup)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the attacker injects Unicode escape sequences (such as \u000a) into the phone_number field of the API request, introducing non-printable characters that create unique variants, bypassing upstream uniqueness checks while being normalized downstream, resulting in multiple accounts tied to the same phone number.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Injecting non-printable Unicode characters into a phone number field is highly abnormal and is a clear attempt to exploit input validation or normalization inconsistencies.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Phone numbers should only contain digits and standard formatting characters. Unicode escape sequences are not valid in this context and should be rejected by input validation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use for Unicode escape sequences in phone numbers in standard web forms or APIs.
key_indicators: Presence of Unicode escape sequences (e.g., \u000a) in phone_number fields during account creation
Multiple accounts with visually identical phone numbers that differ only by encoding
API requests to /dashboard/onboarding/phone/verify containing non-digit or non-printable characters in phone_number

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the attacker uses the recollapse tool via command line to automatically generate and test multiple phone number variants by inserting Unicode escapes and altering positions, automating the process of bypassing uniqueness checks and enabling mass account registration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated fuzzing of input fields to discover and exploit validation bypasses is a common attacker technique and is not part of normal user or developer workflows.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal account creation does not involve automated input mutation, fuzzing, or the use of specialized tools to generate input variants.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Security researchers may use such tools in controlled testing environments, but not in production or user-facing workflows.
key_indicators: Automated input mutation targeting phone_number validation logic
High volume of similar account creation requests with minor input variations
Command-line usage of recollapse or similar fuzzing tools targeting phone number fields

attack_chain.action: Attacker registers an account with a valid phone number.
attack_chain.leads_to: Phone number is associated with an account and receives free credits.

attack_chain.action: Attacker attempts to register additional accounts with the same phone number, but is blocked by uniqueness validation.
attack_chain.leads_to: No free credits granted; uniqueness check triggers.

attack_chain.action: Attacker manipulates the phone_number field by prepending zeros or injecting Unicode escapes to create unique variants.
Attacker automates the process using the recollapse tool to generate and submit many phone number variants.
attack_chain.leads_to: Mass registration of accounts, each receiving free credits.

attack_chain.action: Downstream normalization collapses all variants to the same phone number, but only after credits are granted.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker controls multiple accounts with the same phone number and accumulates free credits.

behavioral_signatures: Multiple account registrations using phone numbers with leading zeros or Unicode escape sequences
High volume of account creation attempts from the same IP address or device fingerprint within a short time frame
API requests to /dashboard/onboarding/phone/verify with non-digit characters or escape sequences in phone_number fields
Patterns of input mutation in phone_number fields across multiple registration attempts
file_indicators: Unusual phone number formats in account database entries (e.g., leading zeros, Unicode escapes)
Logs showing repeated /dashboard/onboarding/phone/verify requests with minor phone_number variations from the same source
Presence of phone_number values that normalize to the same canonical form but are stored as distinct entries
network_indicators: Burst of POST requests to /dashboard/onboarding/phone/verify with similar phone numbers differing only by encoding or formatting
Patterns of account creation from the same network segment or IP address
Unusually high frequency of registration requests containing non-standard phone_number formats
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor account creation API endpoints for phone_number fields containing leading zeros, non-digit characters, or Unicode escape sequences. Implement normalization and validation of phone numbers at the earliest point in the workflow, prior to uniqueness checks. Flag and alert on multiple account registrations tied to phone numbers that normalize to the same value. Correlate high-frequency registration attempts with input mutation patterns and log/alert on attempts to bypass validation using encoding tricks or fuzzed input.
